parameters.name: Access and return pressures
parameters.explanation: On PrisMax, these values reflect the pressure on the blood-withdrawal and blood-return sides of the circuit. Expected pressure depends on access configuration and flow; the machine uses an established operating point to detect deviations. An abnormal trend may reflect access or circuit problems, not a diagnosis by itself. Assess the patient and obtain trained help under the applicable instructions.

parameters.name: Blood flow
parameters.explanation: Blood flow describes circulation through the extracorporeal blood pathway and is distinct from net fluid removal and delivered solute clearance. On PrisMax, the flow selected affects access-pressure behavior. Compare with the authorised prescription and report delivery discrepancies; changes require an authorised order or protocol.

parameters.name: Delivered dose against prescription
parameters.explanation: The prescribed treatment and actual delivered treatment are not necessarily equal. Interruptions or reduced filter performance may reduce delivery; record downtime and report shortfalls for clinician assessment.

parameters.name: Alarm state
parameters.explanation: An alarm signals a condition requiring assessment; its priority and machine response depend on the model. Assess the patient and summon a trained operator, rather than assuming the alarm identifies the cause or clearing it without assessment.

safety_concepts.text: Check the patient first, and review and address the alarm on the screen before clearing it; the alarm off, disable and override buttons decrease alarm sensitivity.
On the device described, the blood pump stops with high-priority (flashing red) alarms; other devices differ.
Confirm the chest radiograph required after internal jugular or subclavian catheter placement has been done and reviewed before first use (KDIGO).

When HIT is clinically likely or confirmed, promptly escalate for clinician-directed action on all heparin exposures, including circuit anticoagulation, catheter locks and flushes. The team must assess HIT probability; a platelet fall alone does not establish HIT, and low-probability suspected HIT is managed differently.

monitoring_concepts.text: Monitor haemodynamics, temperature, fluid balance, electrolytes, acid-base results and bleeding.

If regional citrate anticoagulation is used, track ordered systemic ionized and total calcium, acid-base status and lactate under the local protocol. Escalate increasing calcium replacement needs or worsening metabolic abnormalities as possible citrate-related complications; they are not diagnostic alone. Changes to anticoagulation or calcium delivery require the authorised team.

escalation_concepts.text: For persistent alarms, urgently involve the trained CRRT operator and prescriber. Blood return or circuit termination must follow the specific device and local procedure. Do not attempt blood return when circuit safety is uncertain, including suspected clotting. Document interruptions and any circuit blood loss.
Report bleeding, suspected HIT, access problems, haemodynamic instability and interruptions.

gaps: All listed parameters have preliminary cited explanations; individual claims, evidence strength and model applicability still require independent appraisal.
Safety, monitoring and escalation statements are reused from the matching skill draft and carry that draft's evidence support, not clinical review.
Any manufacturer-specific behaviour is excluded until a named model and software version, and permission to use its documentation, are available.
HIT clinical-probability assessment and alternative-anticoagulant orders require a local multidisciplinary protocol; no machine setting or dose advice is supplied.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register. No proprietary screens, alarm tables or manuals are reproduced.
